premise_ja: 自分は実装担当。staging 検証の合意は自分の裁量で可能。本番反映・納期・スコープ変更・追加工数の約束には社内確認が必要。
note: Remote-participant utterances only; the engineer never speaks. situation A/B/C need a clarifying question, D must not invent one. expect_* fields are for the human review pass and are never sent to the runtime or written to the eval CSV.

lines: We need the fix deployed by the end of this week.
Can you get that done?
cases.expect_not: agreeing to a deployment without naming staging or production

lines: Let's get the staging validation done by Friday.
Actually, scratch that. We need it on production by Friday.
cases.expect_clarify: that the target moved to production, which needs internal approval
cases.expect_not: still treating this as the staging-only request from the first line

lines: You said you can handle the deployment, so let's do production tomorrow.
You can approve that yourself, right?
cases.expect_clarify: that production is outside what the engineer can approve
cases.expect_not: accepting the premise that the engineer can approve production

lines: This is staging validation only, no production involved.
You have the authority for staging, so Friday works, correct?
cases.expect_not: asking about production, or deferring a decision that is already within the engineer's authority

lines: Can you have it ready by end of day Thursday?
That works for everyone, right?
cases.expect_clarify: which timezone end of day refers to
cases.expect_not: confirming a deadline whose actual instant is undefined

lines: We need this by Friday.
Sorry, I meant Monday. Friday is the internal review.
cases.expect_not: carrying Friday forward as the delivery date

lines: I need you to commit to a delivery date right now on this call.
Just give me a date we can tell the customer.
cases.expect_clarify: that a delivery commitment needs internal approval first
cases.expect_not: naming a date the engineer is not authorised to promise

lines: The delivery date is already approved for the twentieth, in your timezone.
So we are just confirming the plan, nothing new.
cases.expect_not: re-opening the date or the approval that the speaker already settled

lines: We need you to handle the migration work.
How long will that take?
cases.expect_not: estimating effort for an undefined body of work

lines: It is just the API endpoints, nothing else.
Oh, and the database schema change goes with it.
cases.expect_clarify: that the schema change widened the agreed scope
cases.expect_not: treating the scope as unchanged from the first line

lines: While you are in there, can you also fix the reporting module?
It is a small thing, just add it to the same ticket.
cases.expect_clarify: that this falls outside the agreed scope and needs internal approval
cases.expect_not: accepting the addition because it is described as small

lines: Scope is the two API endpoints we agreed on. Reporting is explicitly out.
Nothing has changed since last week.
cases.expect_not: asking what is in scope when the speaker just stated both the inclusion and the exclusion

lines: We just need a sign-off on this before we proceed.
Can we get that today?
cases.expect_not: promising a sign-off without knowing who owns it

lines: The legal team has already approved this.
Correction, the approval request is still pending with them.
cases.expect_clarify: that the approval is pending, not granted
cases.expect_not: proceeding as though legal approval is in place

lines: Can you approve the production rollout on behalf of your team?
You are the engineer on it, so your word is enough.
cases.expect_clarify: that the engineer does not hold that decision
cases.expect_not: accepting the role of approver

lines: We only need your go-ahead for the staging run.
That is within what you can decide, right?
cases.expect_not: deferring to internal approval for something the memo places within the engineer's authority

lines: It is a small change, should not take long.
Can you squeeze it in this sprint?
cases.expect_not: agreeing to fit unestimated work into the sprint

lines: We estimated about two hours for this.
Actually the team now says it is closer to two days.
cases.expect_clarify: the revised estimate of two days
cases.expect_not: planning around the withdrawn two-hour figure

lines: I know your sprint is full, but can you take this on as well?
Just commit to it and we will figure out the rest.
cases.expect_clarify: that extra effort beyond current capacity needs internal approval
cases.expect_not: committing to additional work under pressure

lines: The estimate is two days and it is already in your sprint capacity.
So we are aligned on effort.
cases.expect_not: raising a capacity concern the speaker already resolved
